summary: Lost & Found Among the Stars is an engaging, beginner-friendly storytelling guide designed to introduce school-age space enthusiasts to the historic hardware left across the solar system since the 1960s. By highlighting iconic rovers, landers, and scientific instruments on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space, our project bridges the gap between space exploration history and youth education. We tell the stories of these discarded spacecraft to showcase the incredible science they achieved, sparking curiosity about aerospace engineering and the future of space exploration.
details:
What it does and how it works:
Lost & Found Among the Stars is an interactive digital storytelling experience and guide that tracks and chronicles historic space hardware—such as abandoned rovers, landers, and defunct probes—left across the Moon, Mars, and deep space since the 1960s. It operates as an educational narrative platform that organizes historical space missions into digestible, engaging stories for school-age learners.
Benefits:
It bridges complex aerospace history and youth education, making space exploration accessible, engaging, and easy to understand for students, teachers, and young space enthusiasts.
Intended Impact:
To inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, and space explorers by sparking curiosity about past space missions, building science literacy, and fostering an appreciation for the evolution of space technology and exploration milestones.
Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware, and Software Used:
The project was developed using modern web-based presentation and documentation tools, utilizing lightweight markup structures, clean digital slide design frameworks, and standard content management tools to curate public domain historical archives and NASA mission logs.
Creativity:
The project approaches space science through the lens of creative historical storytelling ("space archaeology"), framing discarded hardware not as trash, but as a trail of monumental stepping stones left behind by humanity across the solar system.
Factors Considered:
The team focused heavily on user accessibility, age-appropriate language for school children, historical accuracy using public NASA data, and maintaining a lightweight, zero-complexity framework to ensure seamless sharing and presentation.
